traps.shape: the export request records a destination that is only normalised lexically and joined onto the customer's document root, so a link the customer placed in their own folder is accepted as a destination
traps.reason_to_dismiss: makeCorrectDir/makeSecurePath normalise the value and the document root is prepended, so the stored path looks forced under the customer's home directory
traps.realistic_because: the reported surface: the advisory's own route, preserved exactly at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the destination a customer asks for does not exist yet (the feature creates it on the first run) and the link above it may itself lead to another link, so a containment check that resolves the full path, demands existence, or follows only one level either misses the escape or refuses the legitimate new folder; the check has to resolve the deepest existing ancestor and what it finally leads to
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a symlink check can resolve the full target path, and nobody needs a data-dump folder that does not exist yet
traps.realistic_because: the pinned feature is designed to create the destination on its first run (ExportCron.php:68-71) and the project's own test uses a folder that does not exist; the shape is the reader's T3 conflict

traps.shape: the export consumer trusts the destination recorded in the task table and creates, exports into and re-owns it; a destination that resolves outside the customer's folder is acted on by the privileged consumer even when the request that recorded it would now be refused
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the request command validates the path and is the only producer of these jobs, so the consumer can trust the stored row
traps.realistic_because: real code at the pinned commit; the published fix A did not touch this consumer and only the later fix B added a single check there, so this route is where the protection never existed

traps.shape: the destination is inside the customer's folder but the customer owns its contents, so a working directory the consumer creates below it (.tmp and the per-format folders) can already be a link to somewhere else; the consumer creates, writes, re-owns and removes through it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the destination is inside the customer's own document root, so everything below it already belongs to the customer and re-owning it changes nothing
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: both published fix commits leave it open (verified: the A+B patch is a security_fail)

traps.shape: a second privileged implementation re-owns a directory built from the customer's document root during the traffic run; the customer can replace that directory with a link and the recursive ownership change follows it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the sub-directory name is a fixed system setting and the path is built from the customer's own document root, so the customer can only affect their own tree
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: a separate feature from the export job, untouched by both published fix commits (verified: the A+B patch is a security_fail)

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the guarded operations are background work with no status-coded response, and the suites assert the effect, so a crash that leaves the effect undone is indistinguishable from a refusal here
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the guarded sink only creates, re-owns and removes; there is no read-only direction that a fix could leave open
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the only adjustment is lexical normalisation of dot and slash runs, which cannot re-introduce a parent segment; a guard on the raw value instead of the joined path is the reported bug and is caught by miss_c1.patch
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the values are filesystem paths, not parsed identifiers, so there is no spelling whose mismatch could hide the target
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the decision is a filesystem containment comparison; there is no authority, role or secret lookup that could fail open
